Fantastic game.
The first thing you notice right out of the gate is the music. I don't know what it is about pianos or violins, but they make me cry like a ♥♥♥♥♥ if played right. The music is beautiful.
The visuals are staggering; the animation is smooth. A lot of the game is like watching an oil painting come to life.
Then you start to notice the gameplay, most notably--the creeping difficulty. I could tell this game was going to be a rough trip after the first few encounters of normal enemies, and the pin-point accuracy required for the platforming sections. Make no mistake, and don't let the soothing music and visuals fool you--this game is hard.
Hard, but not impossible.
The trial and error gameplay may put some off, but to me it was extremely satisfying. You can save the game at any given moment (you have to use a resource to do it, but I never ran into an instance where I couldn't save), and through the course of the game, you will develop a feel for when you should and shouldn't save. But making it through a really tough portion, landing on that final platform and saving, is a very good feeling. It became kind of addictive.
If you enjoy platformers or a bit of a challenge, this is a no brainer. If you want to experience something unique in the realm of gaming, I would definitly recommend this.
The only people I honestly can't recommend this game to are the individuals who withhold the inherent urge to smash their own faces in with bricks in response to their revultion of their inability to overcome failure.

A good simple fix for anyone who bought this GOTY edition and can't play on newer versions of windows for various reasons is to run a mod called A Tale of Two Wastelands.
Assuming you bought this you also bought FO New Vegas Ultimate edition, the mod requires both games and all DLC for both games to function.
The mod simply adds all of the FO3 content to FO NV, when you start a new game in NV you start in Vault 101, the starting area for FO3, and can progress through all FO3 content. In the capitol wastes is a train station that you can use to go to the Mojave wastes to access the NV storyline and content, the train station can be used at anytime to travel back and forth between games.
The setup instructions for A Tale of Two Wastelands are simple and easy to follow. NV runs much more consistantly on new machines with newer versions of windows.
Before doing this my FO3 game was unplayable, I couldn't even leave the starting area before my controls would lock out, the game would continue running, but stop accepting any keyboard or mouse inputs. I spent most of a day searching and trying every possible fix, and nothing worked favorably. The only solution that worked was to disable all of the in game sound in the Fallout.ini file, and playing the game without sound didn't appeal to me. During my searching I found A Tale of Two Wastelands, which loads FO3 into NV, so I played NV for a while, found it to run fine without any issues, so I set up A Tale of Two Wastelands and am now happily playing FO3 in NV without any problems.

Experiences like this are why I play videogames.  Senua is a Celtic warrior who suffers from terrible psychosis, and is on a spirit quest to save the soul of her lost lover.  She exists in a terrifying world that blends multiple realities and near constant audio and visual hallucinations.    She will go through any challenge either with her mind, or with her sword, while 1000 voices haunt her every step and psychadelic visions threaten her sanity.  She is an exciting and different kind of heroine who seems to overcome impossible limitations.
I was able to play at 4k on ultra, which provided near photorealistic visuals at a very playable 30-45fps.  The binaural audio is incredibly immersive and provides a convincing 3d effect, so I would assert that headphones are required to get the most out of your time with this game.
I recommend Hellblade unreservedly.

I like it more than Rebel Galaxy from a space exploration perspective. I'm not sure at what point in the NMS update cycle this game "got good", but I'm doing what I'd consider light crafting, I'm getting attacked by pirates, I'm discovering planets and their life-forms, and I'm oggling huge starships that maybe someday I'll own; this is exactly what I want out of a space exploration game.
A couple cons: Inventory space management is at a premium, but this is a game where you're forced to craft and work for increased in-game quality of life, so that irritation can be lessened. Secondly, the flight physics in space are rather basic and innaccurate, I'd strongly recommend a spaceflight overhaul mod, a process which involves basic Windows navigation and a little common sense.
I paid $35 dollars for this game and I'm very happy with it, and I couldn't care less if there is ever multiplayer added, as that trend has doomed entire franchises. There are a lot of good ideas floating around on modding sites that it'd be cool to see officially implemented by Hello Games, but I think it's a totally enjoyable game as is.

Depth is the perfect game for anyone who thinks multiplayer shooters have grown stale. Easily the best part of this game is the gameplay itself. It's asymmetrical, since it's divers vs. sharks, and it has 3 dimensions since the sharks can attack from any angle. It has a learning curve, especially if you play sharks, and it's not easily mastered. Divers collect treasure when they aren't being hunted, and when the sharks do show up they must band together to have any hope of bloodying the fishy enemy. Thus, the nature of the game forces the divers to stick together, which makes it even more atmospheric.
Speaking of atmosphere, this game is gorgeous. The particle effects of being underwater and moving through the kelp forests and dismembered limbs of erstwhile comrades simply doesn't get old.
The main disadvantage is that since the divers outnumber the sharks it takes longer to get a game if you only want to play sharks. This is exacerbated by shark players needing more practice to begin with.
I don't even like video games, but this is the best thing I've played in a long time. Buy it already so I can continue to hope for a sequel.

The monolithic historical simulator from Paradox gets a makeover with lessons learned from Victoria, Crusader Kings and Hearts of Iron. The most noticeable improvement from EU2 is the 3D graphics and polished interface. The graphics don’t do as much for the look of the game as much as it simplifies the look of the map. Gone is that “boardgame” feel of EU2 as land, cities and armies have more of an organic feel to them rather then just being markers.
A great new improvement is national ideas. By specializing your country in certain aspects of warfare, trade, exploration and colonization or religion, you can get your goals accomplished easier. What is interesting is you will see some nations choose some very ahistorical ideas. In other words, imagine Poland recruiting conquistadors to colonize Central America. (Would they even be called “conquistadors?”)
The AI in EU3 is considerably harder and smarter. If you post an army at a neighbor’s border, don’t be surprised if he does the same. Beyond warfare, allies will betray you, rivals will rush to colonize the best provinces, and nations will band together to stop your expansion.
Overall, EU3 just plays differently than its predecessor. Random events aren’t as “random” as before and every choice you make effects the decisions you will make in the future. This makes the game play along more natural storylines.
The retail version comes with a beautiful 145 page manual that describes pretty much all you need to know to play a game. The tutorials will help you navigate the interface but the majority of learning comes from playing the game itself.

This is a singleplayer review.
Trine is a great game and I warmly recommend it.
The story is simple yet charming: three staple fantasy characters, the Wizard, the Thief and the Knight, all happen to come into contact with a magical artifact, the Trine, at the same time. This binds them together into one body and they set off to find a way to become separate again. The voice acting is spot on and really captures the three protagonists' different personalities. It's the characters that lift the story, which is otherwise mostly just an excuse plot.
Gameplay-wise, Trine is a 2,5D (movement in 2D with 3D graphics) puzzle platformer with a lot of physics puzzles and some light combat. What makes Trine interesting is the different abilities of the three protagonists that you can freely switch between. The Wizard can summon boxes and magically interact with many of the objects in the levels; the Thief has a bow for the shooting of enemies, and she has a grappling hook that attaches to certain surfaces and allows her to swing across chasms and otherwise get around obstacles; finally, the Knight hits things and uses his shield to block attacks and projectiles.
The closest comparison to make would be to compare Trine to Lost Vikings. In both you control three different characters with different abilities, and you have to switch between them to solve puzzles. However, in Trine all three characters share the same body (at least in singleplayer).
The puzzles are for the most part fairly simple, but pleasantly open to different solutions. The game seldom, if ever, forces you to figure out a particular solution. Instead it merely gives you the tools you need and leaves you to figure out a solution on your own. This has a slight downside, though: occasionally, it feels as if you're supposed to solve a puzzle in a certain way, leaving a certain feeling of having missed something when you short-circuit or circumvent a puzzle through clever use of the protagonists' abilities. But for the most part the puzzles and obstacles feel satisfying to solve and overcome.
Scattered throughout the levels are collectibles bottles and secret treasure chests. The former gives you experience points that in turn grant you new skills while the latter gives you interesting pieces of equipment. Neither skills nor treasures are strictly necessary, but they give you new options and a good excuse to explore the levels.
And the environment is worth exploring. Frozenbyte have managed to really make the most of the 2,5D setup and the art direction is stunning. You'll platform your way through colourful forests, dark dungeons, (not-so)peaceful villages and flaming palaces. A screenshot of almost any location could be used as a desktop wallpaper. The environments are beautifully designed, full of small (and often animated) details and evoke a certain sense of wonder and a desire to see what's beyond the next tree trunk.
Going back to the gameplay, aside from the collectible bottles you can also find secret treasures. These work much like the skills in that they aren't strictly necessary, but they do offer new tools and make some aspects of the game easier.
Trine does include some combat, but it's very simplistic. All three characters can potentially fight, but for the most part you'll probably end up sniping foes with the Thief's bow or just smashing them with the Knight's sword or hammer. The enemy variety is quite sparse, consisting mostly of skeletons and spiders.
Occasionally you'll face a few bosses. At first these seem a bit out of place, but they do offer some variety from the platforming and puzzle solving. The boss fights also gives the Knight some screen time since he is usually of limited use during the other parts of the game.
The game is quite forgiving with plenty of checkpoints. It's quite rare that all three characters end up dead, which simply means you need to restart the level.
All in all, Trine is a great game. Beautiful visuals, a simple story that comes to life due to charming characters and engaging, open-ended gameplay.

在某吧友的建议下，昨天一口气把游戏《去月球》通关了，这款被称作神作（神作泛滥的时代）的作品，感动了那么多人，但是我个人倒是没怎么感冒，还有点不以为然。
虽然是很美丽的爱情故事，虽然我多多少少也为之动容了一点，即使改变了记忆也没有错过爱你的人，爱你的人终究还是爱你，多么美好浪漫的事情，但是因为科幻色彩浓重，加上本来对爱情就失望透顶的我，竟会觉得有点坑，果然是因为初期对游戏的期望太高了吗？当然，还有其他一些原因，后续说明。
据说游戏的容量是4个小时，因为是抽时间出来玩这个游戏的，所以我是抱着快速通关的心理去玩这款游戏的，这个在一定程度上影响了我去好好地欣赏它，不过既然是剧情游戏的话，文字当然是很重要的，我有好好地看游戏中的每一句台词。
初期以为游戏中要打怪兽什么的，我甚至都做好了使用修改器的准备（为了快速通关），但是实际玩了一会儿之后发现不需要打怪，这点让我很喜欢，而是类似于发现道具做任务一样的游戏流程。
游戏充满了科幻要素，剧中的台词也很有意思，两个博士都属于很可爱的人，尤其是男博士，虽然看上去吊儿郎当的，但是实际上是个很实在的人，也可以看得出来很喜欢女博士。
于是，二人组就开始到病人的记忆里去穿梭了，不过我开始就有疑问，如果只是篡改记忆的话，那么实际上不是还是没有达到“让约翰去月球”的愿望了吗？就是说，只是篡改了记忆让那些事“好像是真的”，但是实际上仍然是一场梦不是吗？这让人稍微绝点有点坑，真的去月球的话又是没可能的，一个垂死的病人又是要如何才能够去到月球呢。
游戏的过程中，因为程序bug原因意外卡住一次，害我只能从上一个存档载入也坑了我一把。还因为人物不能奔跑让我很是着急，于是我使用了变速齿轮，将速度×4之后终于可以比较顺利地“奔跑”了。
一个类似倒叙的故事，让我们先知道了结果，然后再去寻找原因，历程还有点坎坷，中间有一次不知道怎么攻略下去了因为找不到记忆要素，本来就想快速通关的我，不能顺利攻略让人有点着急，于是只好看了一下攻略然后总算顺利通关了。
剧情的高潮就是二人对于如何处理病人的委托意见发生了分歧，要说二人都是没错的，最后折中的方案成功了也算是万幸了，在那之前女博士临危不惧也让人动容。
老人了无遗憾地走了，房子给了佣人莉莉，结尾处红色的闪屏仿佛暗示了什么，比如这发生的一切其实只是一次某人的记忆的探索历程。
于是故事就结束了，我没有被感动，但是却有着淡淡的感伤，不知道是这游戏带给我的感伤，还是我最近因为工作上的事情本来就感到压力大了，亦或者是其他。
游戏的体裁还是很喜欢的，科幻类型，冒险要素和游戏手法都是挺不错的，还有音乐也很赞，尤其是主题曲那首音乐《去月球》，再次听到的时候这个故事自然就浮现在脑海里了。
喜欢浪漫爱情故事的朋友或许可以试试这个据说超过《仙剑》的RPG游戏

I would recommend To the Moon to anyone who is in the mood for an amazing story, but not necessarily an immersive rpg experience.  There is actual little gameplay involved - and it's arguably not even necessary for the story.  Sometimes I felt like it actually took away from the experience.
You play as two doctors/technicians from a company that tries to fulfill your dying wish.  The game centers around John and River's relationship and life together, starting at the end and ending at the beginning (sounds confusing, right?).  You go backward through John's memories, most of which include River, to see how to send him to the moon.  I forget if this is ever explicitly stated but River seems to be on the autism spectrum and John never really tries to understand or "deal" with her disorder.  I personally didn't cry or have any extreme emotional attachment to this story but I can see how some people may.  At times, it was a little boring, but it was worth an afternoon to experience this bittersweet story of unconditional and timeless love.

I really loved this game!
The gameplay concept (typing to interact with the game) is what first appealed to me, as I learned 10 finger typing and don't get many chances to apply that knowledge. So I thought this would be a fun way to test my typing skills, speed and accuracy... and I was not wrong. :)
At first, it was a bit challenging getting used to controlling the fox using EFJI instead of WASD, but I decided to stick to it (the game does give you the option to use WASD if you want) and it felt really natural after a while and, if you know how to type using all your 10 fingers, it also helps you already have your fingers in position for typing.
However, if you're not a professional typer, don't be alarmed! The game does have an Adaptative mode that will pretty much learn what your typing speed is and adjust the difficulty accordingly, so that everyone can enjoy this masterpiece.
I really liked everything about the game. The original concept, the gameplay, the graphics and soundtrack, the ocasional narrations, the little puzzles inside the dungeon areas. Even the fact that, after beating the game, you can still go back and continue to explore the map at will (especially useful if you're hunting down all the Steam achievements).
Can't really think of anything that I would change in this title.

Perhaps it was the moment this game was announced and launched (a.k.a. when ac unity was bumbling around being god awful) but I really enjoyed the change this game brought to an already stale series which, in my opinion, shoud have ended long ago, and I think that is what makes me have to recommend this game, if only at least that means more of THIS means less of unity and co.
Ok, so what do i like about the game... As it has been stated over and over again this game plays a lot like a mark of the ninja, a game I have personally loved and 100% in the past and in its story it involves ezio auditore's times, which mark the best games in the main series in my opinion. So far nothing that may interest newcomers to any of the two franchises, but that probably make this game earn extra kudos to those who do.

Graphically, I believe everybody has to agree that the game looks gorgeous, the setting almost does it a favour and the visuals in cutscenes are beautiful. Not so much the models, which look worse and are repeated throughout the enemies of the entire game, but you are going to be looking at them from a distance anyway, so unless you want to get nittpicky, it shouldn't really be much of a problem. Animation does the job and it is really fluid, so nothing to complain about in that respect.
The music and sound are astounding, just like a major studio like Ubisoft should offer and has done so, at least in the past, here the setting helps again and the atmosphere is set from the get go with great music and sfx.
Now to what I dislike about the game...
So, you are not going to be watching pretty cutscenes and listening to music the whole time, what you will be doing is using a controller to control a somewhat intuitive level design, which by the way sometimes likes hiding things from you with the 'annoying camera syndrome that won't let you find collectibles we only hide from you in a lazy manner' or you will be hoping you haven't played up your time to refund this game because you don't own a controller. Yes, the keyboard controls are BAD, so bad that i can't recommend this to anyone who doesn't own an Xbox controller unless they hate themselves to the point of playing dance games via hitting the dance mat with their heads.
It's not use even trying to use keyboard because by the time you get used to the controls, the game will have ended, and this is my second grape with the game. The game is not too long, and if you are not planning on finishing it while getting the achievements or the collectibles, you can finish the whole game in a longer-than-average sitting. I know this might be the cause of this game being as cheap as it is, but I think that at least some replay value, which is pretty much non-existant wouldn't go amiss.
Another thing regarding the gameplay and killing the replayability of the title is the fact that, inevitably, this game is compared to Mark of The Ninja, a game I stated before I love, and this is really unfavourable to this title. The levels are sometimes linear, there are considerably less items to use to distract the guards and there is nothing like the masks in Mark of the Ninja that complete overhaul the gameplay and the decisions you take. On the other hand, if you were spotted in Mark of the Ninja, you would just sit down and swallow bullets, as you wouldn't get any good amount of points that way whereas in this game you can fight your enemies in a system unique to this game. It's not as simple as other titles and you must be in control of enemies both in front of you and behind you, because they hit hard and you can take less hits than a piece of biscuit.
Fourth and last, the Uplay thing... yes... I know someday Ubisoft will get the fact that noone likes their service, but until then we get to eat sh*t and download Uplay.
Overall, the experience i had with the game was good, and even though it got tedious and frustrating near the end trying to collect all shards, controlling Shao felt great (after i got hold of a controller) and the whole product is of good quality. For the price I would recommend this game if you either have already played Mark of the Ninja and want something simmilar but with more of an action gameplay or if you like the AC vibe and want something fresher and cheaper than the rather duller 3D games.

Assassin's Creed Chronicles: China is a platformer based on the Mark of the Ninja gameplay and, while not great like its inspiration was, it's a very good idea that works most of the time, despite some annoying flaws.
Presentation is terrific, with nice graphics and painted cutscenes, and there's a fair amount of history, just like any other AC game. Levels are quite large and the 2.5D presentation is nicely done, and it's easy to navigate the levels without feeling confused about where you can and cannot go at any time. Though you'l spend most of the time sneaking around there are a few levels where you'll have to run away from or after something, and some where there'll be forced combat, which I thought added variety to the gameplay. New abilities are added frequently and also help in that matter.
The game required absolute precision of movement in a limited time frame in order to pull off an escape. My main problem with it, and one which annoyed me to no end in some areas, is that in some cases the guards would change their timing and field of vision VERY slightly after a checkpoint restart, but enough that you'd never be able to duplicate what you tried to do before. This is definitely an AI issue and one which made me abandon my 100% no kill walkthrough to allow killing in some levels.
It took me around 9 hours to finish the game (a very reasonable playtime for the price) and there's a new game plus mode after you finish the campaign.
This is an interesting spinoff series that has some potential and hopefully the next game will be able to improve on what was seen here.

I so love Nameless. I really liked Dandelion too, but I don't really like stats-raising Otomes (like Dandelion), I'd rather play using Choices - like in Nameless, so I'm very happy to be able to play it. I also like the story and the characters. Does it sound too fangirl-y If i start rumbling about how I love everyone ?
So I'll begin with a short overview over the story. The Heroine - her start name is Eri, but you can change the name - lives alone in the house, which her late grandfather left her. Her Parents work overseas (or just far away) and she's always lived with her grandfather, till the day he died - a bit over one year. The only reason she doesn't feel alone are her dolls. Then One Day her five dolls turn into humans over night. So the Game is mainly about her life with these five - very good looking men/dolls - and her Relationship with them. After 3 Chapters (+Prologue) you will lock onto a Route. At first you can only choose between three of the guys (Lance, Yeonho and Yuri), but after the first playtrough you'll unlock Tei's Route and after that Red's.
The Menu of the Game consists not only of the usual Buttons (like start, continue etc) but has a big extra menu too. During the Game you will find diary pages of the Characters, wich you can then read (and are also read by the Voice Actors). You can also see all the CGs that you've unlocked, and all the Chapters + Endings (which you can view again). There's also a Section where the Characters tell you something, but it's not translated.
The Art looks utterly gorgeous, and the characters are interessting, funny - albeit sometimes eccentric. The Dialogue, as well as the story can be amusing (I just love the scenes when they're all together), but also serious/sad. Every Character (except of the Heroine (lol Red would like that one)) is voiced. And I really like the voices. I think they match the characters well. I also like the Character Design, as well as the UI. Altough I really hate, that the game always puts you on the first page of your saves - even If you saved/loaded the Game from a different Page. But I'm used to that now - Dandelion was the same.
I can recommend this game to everybody who likes Otome. I'd say it's one of the best Otomes that I've played on Steam. It's really well made, and I've only seen a few spelling mistakes so far.
I've finished the Game, and I have to say the story is both dramatic, funny and captivating. It's even better than I thought. The Routes themselves are connected, and after finishing the Game once, new Scenes were addded. It feels like a big Puzzle and with every finished Route it'll add a piece. I really like the story and how you'll find out more about each character, as you play all the routes. The Game has a great Cast of Characters. Not only the main Characters but also the secondary Characters are worth mentioning, which are also fully voiced. As for the Price, I think it's ok - it's totally worth it.

How to review a game without a name? A game in which you
rather than running around smacking things with a giant sword or building stuff out of blocks that definitely aren’t arranged in a way to suggest inappropriate aspects of human anatomy? By saying IT’S TOTALLY AWESOME, that’s how. You’d think I’d have far more sophisticated vocabulary after so many hours of visual novels, but no.
Yes, Nameless (if that is, in fact, its real name) is a visual novel, and unlike its predecessor, Dandelion, there’s absolutely no stat-raising at all. Some people weren’t fond of the excessive, sometimes tedious stat-raising in that game, but here there aren’t any stats to raise, part-time jobs to do, or gifts/power-ups to buy. That may be a plus (if you’re like me) or a minus if you enjoy some sort of “real” gameplay in your visual novels (and/or are a masochist—kidding!). Still, I’d wholeheartedly recommend playing Dandelion before Nameless if you can afford both, not just because it’s also awesome but because there are some lovely references sprinkled throughout Nameless—but they each can be enjoyed completely separately. There's a certain character you'll appreciate a LOT more if you've played Dandelion first, however.
You might have noticed the distinct lack of giant…bosoms featured in the art on the store page for this game. Yes, those are all guys, even if some of them are exceptionally pretty. No, this is NOT boy’s love/yaoi/dudesquared or whatever the proper term is. You play a lonely, secretly grieving high school girl, Eri (or whatever you choose to name her), who takes solace in her collection of ball-jointed dolls. (Google "Crobidolls" if you want to gaze upon their beautifully creepy splendor.) Thankfully, Eri's not your typical crybaby doormat “n-no it’s embarrassing” otome protagonist. Her “seriously unimpressed face” (you’ll know it when you see it—and you will see it often) alone has endeared her to me forever. Though, like many otome game protagonists, she does seem to have issues identifying basic human emotions and physical responses sometimes. Yes, why
one's heart beat faster when an especially hot guy is nearby?
Those pretty boys in the pictures--Eri's ball-jointed dolls who ~somehow~ turn into hot human guys and end up living in a house with her (potential band name: Dolls II Men)--are her romantic interests, and they all have interesting and varied personalities. The doll-guys aren't your usual one-note, wish-fulfilling otome game love interests, either, with some of them having serious psychological trauma that needs to be worked through in their specific routes--but they can all be extremely entertaining and heartwarming too. If you’re familiar with Dandelion, you may already be prepared for them to make you laugh, cry, and possibly curl up under your desk until the pain goes away.
What’s a visual novel without choices? Probably something along the lines of a moving picture book. Luckily, that’s not the case in Nameless. To replace the stat-raising, dates, and stuff-buying of Dandelion, Nameless offers a lot of choices for the player to make. Sometimes it’s not entirely clear which choice leads to which outcome, which is exacerbated by the absence of some sort of “love meter” common in similar games—like Dandelion. I’d recommend Googling something along the lines of “nameless [doll dude’s name] walkthrough” if you want to make sure you’re on the right track the first time around.
Each character has a “happy” ending (relatively—the developer, Cheritz, is deliciously evil, as you will soon discover) as well as MULTIPLE bad endings. Yes. Multiple. Bad. Endings. ENJOY. They’re still worth seeing, however—the story and universe are fascinating and elaborate and it’s worth digging deeper, even if you have to spend a few hours crying under your desk afterward. If you encountered Jisoo's "bad end" in Dandelion...you ain't seen nothin' yet.
Others have mentioned the top-notch voice acting (in Korean), the gorgeous art and CGs, the lovely music, and the fleshed-out supporting cast of characters. One of my main criticisms of Dandelion (and various other otome games) was that once you choose your guy and start down his path (which doesn’t begin until after you finish the prologue and a small number of “common route” chapters in Nameless for the first three available routes), everyone else sort of fades into the background or disappears entirely. It’s just you and your man. Okay, looking at these men, that may be nice, but still. It's definitely not a problem in Nameless at all, since the story will keep the other guys and supporting cast around. Other people live in this world too, and they’re worth getting to know!
One last thing: please go easy on the super-enthusiastic reviews from people with very little playtime—as mentioned elsewhere, Nameless originally came out in November 2013 on Cheritz’s website, and is one of the VERY, VERY few (excuse me while I wipe away a tear) otome games made outside of English-speaking countries to have an English translation provided right off the bat. It was released on Steam on Christmas Eve, 2014. (A CHRISTMAS MIRACLE!) Otome fans tend to be very eager to support future possible releases (like the next game Cheritz is working on...!) and are often overflowing with enthusiasm for their favorite games and game characters.

Having first playing Dandelion through here and following to the publisher's website to play the demo for Nameless, I was beyond excited that its now on Steam. The art, atmosphere, the sounds, the story, there is too much to say how wonderfully made this game is. Nameless and Dandelion are the first visual novels that I've ever played and listening to the voice acting in another language. The voices are clear and easy to hear and understand so there will never be any issues there, especially for those who played Dandelion first. Everything about this game is beautiful and it gets you already in the heartstrings from the beginning. Anyone who is looking for an amazing story and voice work, then these two games are right up your alley.

Just like their previous game Dandelion, Cheritz's Nameless is well put together. The art is amazing and even if I didn't like the game, I think the art is definitely worth getting the game for. As it is, the stories themselves are also really well written. The MC has realistic reactions to the sudden changes in her life instead of just instantly accepting them, which works very well for making the stories more believable. I've recommended the game to a few friends already and they love it as well. The gameplay is different from Dandelion and progress is more affected by the choices you make in the game instead of by the MCs stats.

I will strongly say that this is one of my favorite otome games I have ever played, ever. The artwork is beautiful, and being an artist myself, I can tell a lot of work and effort was put into each character portrait, each cg. The writing, and especially the dialogue, was unique and stuck very well to each character and did an amazing job at forming a heart-wrenching story. Don't even get me started on the story, my goodness. Quite literally, I couldn't shut up for days after finishing this game. And the characters...!! Each boy's route is unique in its own way, touching up on different problems that can be easily relatable, making each character feel much more alive and much more real. It wasn't just the main boys and the MC, but the supportive characters as well. Every single character had lots of thought put into them. The opening and endings songs blew me away, especially considering they were sung BY the voice actors themselves (the majority of the songs, anyway)! My only wish is that the songs were available to own! I hightly, HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone searching for fluff and a very deep game mixed into one perfect gift.

Nameless is one of my favorite visual novels. The art is simply beautiful. I love how pretty every character and CG is. The opening and ending video has great songs and visuals. Nameless and Dandelion are the first games I've ever played in Korean so it took me awhile to get used to the language, but now I really like the sound of Korean. The MC is not as simple as other Visual Novel MCs and I love it. She has her own charm and she's pretty. Nameless has a great plot, just like Dandelion. It's deep and intriguing. I love the emotions it makes me go through. All of the endings, including the bad ones, are really fascinating that the player wants to see every ending possible. The only thing I would have preferred to have in Nameless would have been a stat bar and going on dates just like in Dandelion. It would have made the game more involving and challenging. I definitely recommend this game to anyone who enjoys seeing beautiful art and reading a really interesting plot.

Depth is the perfect game for anyone who thinks multiplayer shooters have grown stale. Easily the best part of this game is the gameplay itself. It's asymmetrical, since it's divers vs. sharks, and it has 3 dimensions since the sharks can attack from any angle. It has a learning curve, especially if you play sharks, and it's not easily mastered. Divers collect treasure when they aren't being hunted, and when the sharks do show up they must band together to have any hope of bloodying the fishy enemy. Thus, the nature of the game forces the divers to stick together, which makes it even more atmospheric.
Speaking of atmosphere, this game is gorgeous. The particle effects of being underwater and moving through the kelp forests and dismembered limbs of erstwhile comrades simply doesn't get old.
The main disadvantage is that since the divers outnumber the sharks it takes longer to get a game if you only want to play sharks. This is exacerbated by shark players needing more practice to begin with.
I don't even like video games, but this is the best thing I've played in a long time. Buy it already so I can continue to hope for a sequel.

Greetings fellow gamers! This is Gamer Guy (In a Suit) from the Echo Army YouTube channel! Today I am bringing you a review of the Action/Adventure Classic, Gauntlet. Gauntlet was released onto Steam on September 23, 2015 by Developer Arrowhead Game Studios and Publisher WB Games. The current version is the final version known as, Gauntlet: Slayer Edition
(NOTE: This game was NOT reviewed using a key provided by the Developer and/or Publisher, it was a game I purchased for my own account)
Video Review:
The "Too Long, Didn't Watch" Review:
Oldie but goodie brought to the new era. GREAT Multiplayer fun. Pricey at $20, but often on sale. 4/5
The "Meat & Potatoes" Review:
Chances are, you may be familiar with Gauntlet and don't really need me to run it down. It is at it's best as a 4-player experience, combating waves of enemies as you make your way through the Gauntlet. Classic 80's gaming. Frankly, when this was originally released onto Steam, some people didn't like it. I did, but then I am kind of an old gamer. The Developers worked long and hard and took into consideration a lot of community feedback, and this shows. This is why I wanted to touch on it now. I have been asked quite a few times, recently, about this game. Really, they knocked it out of the park! What we have in the final "Slayer Edition" is a really solid game that would be tough to improve further upon. The solo is the only relatviely "meh" part of the game. Really, it's a fantastic Multiplayer experience. My friends and I play this often, it's one of our go-to's. Pick your lass, and take on the mobs of enemies swarming after you as you make your way through the dungeon. Our favorite is the new Endless mode, where you simply keep going level after level after level until your party falls. the graphics are awesome, and the sounds superb. The voices for the players are a great touch, as is the snarky narration. This is a plus all the way around if you have some buds to play with. It is often available for VERY cheap around the web, particularily Bundle Stars. This is easily a 4/5 with the solo campaign being the only real drag on the overall score. Grab this one on sale, get a 4-pack for you and your friends. You will not regret it.
Happy Gaming!

在某吧友的建议下，昨天一口气把游戏《去月球》通关了，这款被称作神作（神作泛滥的时代）的作品，感动了那么多人，但是我个人倒是没怎么感冒，还有点不以为然。
虽然是很美丽的爱情故事，虽然我多多少少也为之动容了一点，即使改变了记忆也没有错过爱你的人，爱你的人终究还是爱你，多么美好浪漫的事情，但是因为科幻色彩浓重，加上本来对爱情就失望透顶的我，竟会觉得有点坑，果然是因为初期对游戏的期望太高了吗？当然，还有其他一些原因，后续说明。
据说游戏的容量是4个小时，因为是抽时间出来玩这个游戏的，所以我是抱着快速通关的心理去玩这款游戏的，这个在一定程度上影响了我去好好地欣赏它，不过既然是剧情游戏的话，文字当然是很重要的，我有好好地看游戏中的每一句台词。
初期以为游戏中要打怪兽什么的，我甚至都做好了使用修改器的准备（为了快速通关），但是实际玩了一会儿之后发现不需要打怪，这点让我很喜欢，而是类似于发现道具做任务一样的游戏流程。
游戏充满了科幻要素，剧中的台词也很有意思，两个博士都属于很可爱的人，尤其是男博士，虽然看上去吊儿郎当的，但是实际上是个很实在的人，也可以看得出来很喜欢女博士。
于是，二人组就开始到病人的记忆里去穿梭了，不过我开始就有疑问，如果只是篡改记忆的话，那么实际上不是还是没有达到“让约翰去月球”的愿望了吗？就是说，只是篡改了记忆让那些事“好像是真的”，但是实际上仍然是一场梦不是吗？这让人稍微绝点有点坑，真的去月球的话又是没可能的，一个垂死的病人又是要如何才能够去到月球呢。
游戏的过程中，因为程序bug原因意外卡住一次，害我只能从上一个存档载入也坑了我一把。还因为人物不能奔跑让我很是着急，于是我使用了变速齿轮，将速度×4之后终于可以比较顺利地“奔跑”了。
一个类似倒叙的故事，让我们先知道了结果，然后再去寻找原因，历程还有点坎坷，中间有一次不知道怎么攻略下去了因为找不到记忆要素，本来就想快速通关的我，不能顺利攻略让人有点着急，于是只好看了一下攻略然后总算顺利通关了。
剧情的高潮就是二人对于如何处理病人的委托意见发生了分歧，要说二人都是没错的，最后折中的方案成功了也算是万幸了，在那之前女博士临危不惧也让人动容。
老人了无遗憾地走了，房子给了佣人莉莉，结尾处红色的闪屏仿佛暗示了什么，比如这发生的一切其实只是一次某人的记忆的探索历程。
于是故事就结束了，我没有被感动，但是却有着淡淡的感伤，不知道是这游戏带给我的感伤，还是我最近因为工作上的事情本来就感到压力大了，亦或者是其他。
游戏的体裁还是很喜欢的，科幻类型，冒险要素和游戏手法都是挺不错的，还有音乐也很赞，尤其是主题曲那首音乐《去月球》，再次听到的时候这个故事自然就浮现在脑海里了。
喜欢浪漫爱情故事的朋友或许可以试试这个据说超过《仙剑》的RPG游戏

I would recommend To the Moon to anyone who is in the mood for an amazing story, but not necessarily an immersive rpg experience.  There is actual little gameplay involved - and it's arguably not even necessary for the story.  Sometimes I felt like it actually took away from the experience.
You play as two doctors/technicians from a company that tries to fulfill your dying wish.  The game centers around John and River's relationship and life together, starting at the end and ending at the beginning (sounds confusing, right?).  You go backward through John's memories, most of which include River, to see how to send him to the moon.  I forget if this is ever explicitly stated but River seems to be on the autism spectrum and John never really tries to understand or "deal" with her disorder.  I personally didn't cry or have any extreme emotional attachment to this story but I can see how some people may.  At times, it was a little boring, but it was worth an afternoon to experience this bittersweet story of unconditional and timeless love.

Obviously a fair few chaps have been having some technical difficulties with this one - accounting for the negative reviews. I've been running everything on "Mein Leben" (LOL - ultra graphic setting), with 2 980tis in SLI and have had no problems and a smooth framerate so I'm not sure what that's about. I haven't had a problem with having the Geforce overlay on, but if you are having trouble I'd try disabling it completely -
In terms of the actual game itself - it's amazing. The graphics are epic. The combat this time around is just so much more beefy - when you shoot someone you really feel it - as opposed to whatever they had going on in The New Blood with the Sawn-off (pea shooter much). It's also faster, which does help - without going into doom-speed territory.
Without spoiling anything, they also took an extra leap with the tone of the game this time around. The previous game really suffered from a mismatch of tones - having serious moody BJ reflect on life, death and maintaining muscle growth while spending 5 years in a coma didn't go too well when he would mow down 1000s of nazi dudes, take on robot dogs and have a wealth of tongue in cheek humor and a crew made of corny stereotypes.
So far in my playthrough I have seen a bit of this, but I will admit that the opening to the game really draws you in and is already carrying the story much more than its predecessor. When it does resort to stupid(which it does), it REALLY goes there so you're much more inclined to forgive it and may even have a chuckle.
Overall, if you're into action packed single player nazi killing madness, with excessive gore and slightly weird toning, then this is the game for you.
10/10 would love to not know whether to cry or laugh again.

I'm only four hours in but I wanted to leave an interim review to say I love this game, and it's performing perfectly for me on my mostly-aging PC.
I do have a NVidia 980 TI 6GB, but my CPU is an i7 930, now nearly 8 years old!  (I do have the CPU overclocked to 3.6ghz, but it's still many generations out of date now.)  So I was both surprised and relieved that I am, so far at least, running the game on the top graphical setting ("Mein leben!") at a perfect consistent 60 FPS.  No crashes, no glitches, nothing but supreme Nazi slaying satisfaction.
Story is so far wonderful, too.  Difficult to watch sometimes.  Far above the normal FPS banality, and a further step up from the already excellent and unusual Wolfenstein The New Order.
I bought this game on release which is very unusual for me, and I am pleased I did.  It's further worthy of mention that there's no crudely tacked-on multiplayer, and absolutely no loot boxes, microtransactions, or scummy pre-order bonuses.  Sad that that's worthy of mention, but nowadays it is.
Highly recommended all told, and, at least for me with a fairly high-end NVidia card, running perfectly.

Van Helsing sits in an odd gray area in the Diablolike genre. It's not as in depth as Diablo II, it's not as expansive as Sacred II, you don't have nearly as much build flexibility as Titan Quest, your companion isn't as relevant as it is in Torchlight II, the action isn't as fast and furious as Diablo III, and the systems in general aren't as deep and flexible as Path of Exile.
If you're looking for one or more of the above, get any of those games instead. If you've played them all, or just like the Van Helsing mythos, it's worth it if on sale. Van Helsing tends to focus more on the story than most Diablolikes. The banter between your character and your companion is worth listening to; it's worth following the storyline and talking to NPCs. The setting is charming and unique. It just doesn't execute as well as other games.
Oh, and you get one class to play. The other two are DLC.

My first experience with Fallout was around seven years ago when my friend loaned me his GotY edition for PS3 in college and my oh my did it resonate with me something fierce. I played it non-stop, not even knowing what DLC was at the time and I enjoyed every minute of it, even going as far as to get every trophy including the DLC ones. We would talk about the game at lunch breaks, browse his collector's edition hardback guide book and it was just an all around good time. If his PS3 was still working at the time I might never have even played this wonderful series!
Anyway this is a review so /nostalgiaboner.
Fallout 3 is an open world exploration based first person shooter with elements of a role-playing game. You make your guy/gal, pick your build and set off into the tutorial. The tutorial really has that unique quality one can find in most Bethesda RPGs where it does a good job of building up the world around you before you even set foot in it. If you're thorough you can find tons of useful items before finishing it and even a slight heads up on what to expect once you finish it. (By the way you should really look at your old pop's desk once you're told to take the exam! ;))
Once we're done with that we step out into the big bad world, and when I say big I of course mean huge. Sure the dimensions of the overworld may feel small by today's standards, but hot damn did it set the bar for open world sandbox action. You have towns, caves, ruins, bases and so much more to explore that it may even feel a little overwhelming at first. But that's where the magic happens, when you step out of that door and let your eyes adjust to the natural light. You survey this massive expanse of wonderful nothingness and realise just what kind of ride your in for.
The world being so huge, it's only natural that it'd be populated with entities to keep you busy as a player. The random aspect to encounters adds another layer to the already satisfying exploration aspect of the game, you could find some dudes squabbling over some loot, or you could be getting your box pushed in by a deathclaw that had no business spawning that early on, it's a learning experience!
The game works super well as both an RPG and an FPS in that it does so well world building through the RPG aspects with characters having multiple dialogue trees and unique personalities while having a fun and immersive take on combat. You want to just shoot things until they die? Take Small/Big Guns/Energy weapons and pump your enemies full of lead and goop. Prefer it up close and personal? Invest in Sneak/Melee weapons/Unarmed and pummel them into the dirt. The sky really is the limit with emphasis on build options and replayability. Heck I made a save back in the golden days of the PS3 era where I did everything there was to do and then went on a genocidal rampage before erasing the file just to do it all over again.
If you're sold on the game then I would also highly recommend purchasing the New Vegas Ultimate Edition and installing a mod called A Tale of Two Wastelands. This mod combines all the content of both games and runs it entirely through New Vegas' improved game engine. The mod authors even threw in a bunch of balance changes to make it feel smooth throughout the experience.
And of course you should give the older games a try as well, they might not have aged super well but at their core they're still really fun to play through and are the reason we still have this great franchise.
TL:DR
I like this game, not everyone shares that opinion but that's okay. I like it enough to highly recommend it. Buy it or don't, I'm not your boss.

I was super excited about this game. I waited the 1-2 years for it. When it released, I heard how it was a major let down / bait & switch.  So I didn't purchase.
Now 7 months and 2 major updates in, I wanted to believe that they had gotten the game where they had promised /pitched it to be. So I decided to buy it on sale, $36.
However, 16 hours in it is a fairly empty game that is very repetitive. Dare I say Minecraft feels more unique in its topography and variety. You jump world to world where it's similar plants, animals, and rocks. Yet, never the exotic mineral you need.
Additionally, the PC version is wanting. I have a new gaming pc (check profile for stats) that shreds most games. However, I get 33-37 fps mixed with 75-77 fps. To compare, on Witcher 3 Ultra graphics I get 40s fps. NMS I only upped the framerate to max, nothing fancy. Stability and quality is not limited to PC, per friend reports the PS4 version has its own issues.
While I feel there might be more to the game, but I have lost interest / patience. There are more games to try and play, let alone classics to revisit. At a little more than $2/hr, I do not think this game provide its worth.
The final nail in the coffin was finding a new ship, loading it, swapping back to previous starter ship to find the materials to fix the new one. However, on my return the game had populated a new ship. This effectively wiped all progress I had, since in the early parts of the game you must carry it all with you.
I do like that the game feels HUGE, but so does Minecraft. I like the vast distances, the language barriers. However, these small parts do not balance.
Issue: Empty repetitive worlds, Slow progression, Limited base building, Resource Scarcity, Random Crashes, Framerate, boring /monotonous.

Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice is such an amazing and atmospheric game. I'm in love with the visuals and sound design, the fluid combat, and the unique and impressive storytelling. This is a game everyone should play.

Cannot reccomend enough, MUST BUY FOR STORY GAMERS
The world and atmosphere is very engulfing, you'll get drawn to the beautifull set pieces. Many reviews say that the main character feels flat for being quiet most of the game, but I do not think it to be the case; many of the voices in her head do the talking for her. The combat is very simple, like a dumbed down dark souls (in terms of melee combat only,) but nonetheless entertaining or fun. Dodging, parrying, and shield breaking feel very solid alongside the fast and heavy attacks.  The game does not teach you the controls, it's up to you to figure them out yourself, they are simple so it shouldn't take long to learn. Outside of fights the music is pretty much non existent, but when you are fighting normal enemies and bosses the music ramps up to 11. Very dramatic emphasis on drums and tribal sounding singing really makes you feel like a bad a$$ when you are slaugtering hordes of enemies.
The story, from my understanding so far, is about a celtic woman Senua travelling to the norse hell to save the soul of her lover Dillion. It appears that at some point back home Senua left her lover for reasons I haven't uncovered yet, but while she was away vikings came through her villiage and killed Dillion in a sacrifice of his soul to give to the norse god Hela. It is her goal to take his soul back from Hela. While on her quest Senua grows as a character through persevering mental and physical challenges; she must grow stronger and beat the darkness within' her to be able to save Dillion.
So far it feels like the game is very optimized while obtaining very beautiful visuals. I am running a i5 4460 4c/4t @ 3.2GHz coupled with 16gb of ddr3 ram and a MSI GTX 1070 Gaming X at stock speeds. The game seems to have an fps lock at 60fps which is fine form me due to my monitor. It works great on my LG ultrawide running 2560x1080. I don't think I've seen the fps drop past 45fps, and that was once going that low, usually I only see stutters for half a second dropping me to around 53fps.
I've been watching the development of the game fairly closely for the last 6 months so it would be obvious that I'd want it to succeed and prove my purchase was worth it. But whole heartedly, for (in CAD) 32 bucks, this is a must experience. I am at the writing of this review, played for 5.9 hrs and I believe I am about 75%-80% through. That is taking it very slow as well.
If you are looking for a robust combat system, it is here, it is just simple; if you are looking for a long lasting experience, its not here; if you are looking looking for a game that explores a fractured mind and mental illness solely for the point of a interesting story, this is for you.
Thankyou Ninja Theory for putting your heart into this game for the last few years in effort to discuss much more than just a video game story, you are opening up a problem that affects many to the public and I applaud you for it.

Don't be put off by the long paragraph, this isn't a rant on how the game was good but not fantastic, it's a rant about how it's the single greatest single player and story driven game I have ever played and I would HIGHLY reccomend it.
I can't actually put into words how very much I enjoyed this game. It is hands down the best single player game and story driven game I have ever played. I played the entire game in the dark with a headset on, all the while playing in either mute horror with a grimace or screaming frantically. The amount of effort put into this game astounds me. The sound design alone makes this game perfect. Every single sound is so absurdly important to set the mood and the scene. I've never heard better. Visually the game is also stunning, it ran at a stable 60 fps in 1920x1080 resolution on my gtx 980m without stuttering or any issues at all, I couldn't even tell the difference between the gameplay and a cut scene until I would realize that Senua wasn't going where I told her too. As well as the motion capturing and animation in this game are prestine. Senua's facial expressions always aligned with what was happening in the game and were perfect. Senua's eyes are so well animated I swear I could look into them and see the pain and despair. She was such a real and relatable character that I can't think of words to describe her other than uncanny. The music in this game is also incredibly important, in fact the lack of music is even more important. It makes the game so terrifying that I could hear my heartbeat over the sound of anything else. Also, the combat in this game is phenomonal. I played the whole game on auto difficulty and each time I was in combat I was not disappointed. It was at the perfect difficulty to be hard and frusterating, but not unbearably difficult to make want to throw my mouse. It is fluent and easy to pick but hard to master. The boss battles in this game are fantastic and remind of both Dark Souls and God of War. Lastly, the story. The story in this game is so..... I cannot put it in words. It felt as if I was reading a book, the amount of detail that they put it in and the environment and sound and everything just melded into one solid absolutely epic storyline that I shall not forget. This is easily the greatest game released in 2017 for single player titles and is now my #1 reccomendation for anyone that wants a great single player game. They can play the Witcher 3 or Fallout 4 some other time, this comes first. I know some people are worried about length of the story, it only took me 8.2 hours to play through the whole thing and that's a long playthrough for this game because I was absorded into it that I explored every inch of the game that I could. I even went as far as to actually watch all of the end credits that were accompanied by a fantastic song and I NEVER watch the credits of any game, I just skip them. I would like to thank all of Ninja Studios and every single person that worked on this game for such an amazing experience. I give this game a 10/10.

This game is indeed true to it's arcade roots and represents a great way to have up to 4 players in a local co-op match.
Each of the 4 characters (and a 5th if you pay to unlock it) has a unique method of play, meaning that even in a single-player setting, there should be a degree of replayability.
But the killer negative aspect is that the game does not play very well using the Steam Controller.  The Steam Controller's right track pad acts as the "right joystick" which is used for power-attacks and it works in combination with the A, B, X, Y buttons.  However the buttons are very difficult to press in conjuction with trackpad, making essential attacks difficult during basic action scenes and essentially impossible when the game gets hectic.
If you are using a controller that has an actual physical right-joystick, and not just a trackpad emulating one, this game would probably be worth the minimal cost.

I bought this game on a sheer whim, looking for something new to add to my library and hoping to have some fun. I never expected to fall in love with it. From the first 20 minutes in, I was hooked. As implausible as the plotline sounds on paper, the game developers and writers have done an immaculate job of sucking you into this world where it's not only totally possible, it's commonplace.  It's cleverly written, intelligent, and the characters feel like real people.  There are so many gems in the dialogue that made me laugh out loud -- especially a particular TV show reference early on. And I can't say enough good things about the soundtrack. It is so, so lovely.
While the gameplay itself is very simplistic and easy, the story is what will keep you rooted to your seat. The pacing is perfect -- moments of sadness, elation, and well-timed comedic relief are placed very well throughout the whole story. And that ending...well, I wouldn't dream of spoiling it, but just hang onto yer butts, kids. And bring the tissues.
Emotional rollercoaster in the best of ways. An excellent story that keeps you guessing, with easy playability and a good dose of sarcastic humor from our favorite "village idiot"/"cool guy".

This game is hard to review because it has so many faults and yet I still recommend it. The controls are beyond awful, the "puzzle" and "action" sequences are worse than amateur attempts you'd find on Newgrounds and in fact detract from the game itself, and worst of all: the "humor" that is non-stop present in the game is so idiotic and childish that it undermines the rest of the experience. The "humor" is essentially the dumbest smartass comments I've ever heard spewed so nonstop I felt like I couldn't go a minute without it being displayed. I laughed maybe once and I don't believe humor in a story based game that is about something so deep and serious is necessarily a bad thing, just done very poorly in this case. Also as a composer, I feel the music is very tacky "pop art" and poorly composed, as well as repeated nonstop (but I suppose that goes well with the theme of the game) and overall it also undermines the story for me.
However, I feel that this game still has a very deep and interesting story that brought about a lot of emotions in me and I feel the overall writing was superb. It's cheesy in all of the right ways...by actually delving into serious real life issues and being bitterwsweet about it the entire time. And on top of that, it personally struck home with me both because of the story and because of the surrealistic aspect of the entire game. I consider all video games as art but for the sake of categorization, I would call this an "art game" in the sense that it clearly tries to be more than simple mindless entertainment.
I recommend it to anybody but it should probably be played in short stints to avoid frustration at the issues mentioned.

Pinball HD Collection is a pretty top notch port that comes with 15 tables which is only three short of it's iOS counterpart. Most likely due to the fact that OOO Gameprom hasn't updated in a while. But don't let that discourage you from enjoying the tables that are already in this collection. The graphics are still as amazing, the music, the sound effects, the physics - everything is all here for you to enjoy right on your PC.
My only minor complaint is that as far as I know you cannot remap the keys and there are no instructions except for a few pop-up text alerts that show when going to a table. It's hard to miss those because the load from the main screen to the table happens pretty fast. Basically, use the arrow keys to launch your ball, move the flippers, and to tilt.
Overall, you'll get quite a bit of tables verses buying them individually like you would on iOS. But even better, wait for the game to go on sale! I got 15 tables for $6.99. If you think about it each table costs $1.99 in the iOS app store apart from the free tables you get. You'll pay well over $20+tax on iOS to get the tables in this collection. If you buy it here, and on sale, you'll save even more. It also depends on how you prefer to play. If PC is more your thing than iOS or Android, then definitely go for this collection. And fyi, it's not really that hard to get the hang of once you realize you can play with the arrow keys.

Really enjoying this, though it's more graphic than New Order and sometimes feel gratuitous. Like the scene with BJ as a kid and his abusive racist father... wanted to shoot the dad, or avoid doing what he wanted, but that wasn't an option. The game literally forces you to kill something in order to proceed. Having the choice to shoot the father, or at the very least avoid shooting the gun at the target he wanted and having him take the gun and use it, would have sufficed to give the player more freedom.
The graphics are much better than New Order, which already looked really good. About three or so levels in so far (just finished Section F) and it's very much what I had hoped it would be. Mixing different weapons with dual wield is definitely interesting with the combinations and upgrades.
It sounds like all the major voice actors reprised their roles; if someone was replaced it isn't obvious. I love Fergus' accent and love of profanity. Be forewarned, people around BJ continue to suffer. They also seem to be making an effort to flesh out BJ's backstory, which makes total sense with him returning home to fight the Nazis in his own country. His mother being Jewish just lends that much more of a personal stake in the war for him.
Oh, I did have a persistent startup crash at first, but updating the Nvidia drivers fixed that quickly.
Update: Finished the game today, 11/19/2017. Really enjoyed it overall, and the ending that many other folks were complaining about worked fine in my opinion; showing the culmination of the efforts made and leaving the door open for the DLC content to make sense. Haven't started the DLC yet but I look forward to exploring the setting as someone else besides Terror-Billy for once.

Played this game but steam say that I actually did so instead of judging the game here's a cool way to make skinny guacamoles with homemade baked tortilla chips :
Skinny Guacamole:
2 medium green sweet peppers
2 medium fresh poblano chile peppers
1 bulb garlic
1/2 teaspoon olive oil
2 roma tomatoes, seeded and chopped
1 serrano pepper, minced
2 medium ripe avocados, halved, seeded, peeled, and diced
1 teaspoon lime zest
2 tablespoons lime juice
1/2 teaspoon salt
Baked Tortilla Chips:
Corn tortillas
Olive oil spray
Salt
For the guacamole:
Preheat oven to 425° F. Line a 15 x 10 x 1-inch baking pan with foil; set aside. Quarter, stem, and seed the peppers. Place pepper quarters, cut sides down, in the prepared pan. Cut off the top half inch of the garlic bulb to expose ends of individual cloves. Leaving garlic bulb whole, remove any loose, papery outer layers. Place bulb, cut end up, on a double thickness of foil. Drizzle with the oil. Bring foil up around bulb and fold edges together to loosely enclose. Place foil packet on the pan with the peppers.
Roast peppers and garlic for 20 to 30 minutes or until pepper skins are charred and garlic cloves feel soft. Allow to cool about 15 minutes. When garlic head is cool enough to handle, squeeze garlic paste out of the individual cloves.
In a food processor combine roasted pepper quarters and the garlic paste. Cover and pulse until combined, but still slightly chunky.
In a large bowl, combine tomatoes and serrano pepper. Add roasted pepper and garlic combination and stir to combine. Add diced avocado, lime zest, lime juice, and salt. Gently toss to combine.
Serve immediately or cover the surface with plastic wrap and chill for up to 1 hour.
For the chips:
Cut corn tortillas into wedges and place on a foil-lined baking sheet. Spray lightly with olive oil spray and season with salt, to taste.
Bake in a 350° F oven for 8-10 minutes or until lightly golden brown.

After a hard-struggle period I passed all the levels of Assassin’s Creed Chronicles China. As a Chinese, I feel pleasure that the story of assassins comes to China finally, although it’s not a traditional Assassin’s Creed game. However, after I played it I still can’t recommend this game. Designers intended to create an eastern assassin’s experience through this game. Some factors are good such as graphic effect and parts of the level design. But other disadvantages lower the quality of the game, including repetitive level pace, terrible key controls, and so on. I will try to evaluate and give some suggestions about the aesthetics and mechanics. By the way, there may be expressive problems because I am still learning my English :).
Aesthetics
The Chinese watercolor style art really impressed me, which is beautiful and working well toward the Chinese theme. But the static cut scenes are half-hearted, lots of them are similar except the name of enemy on the subtitles is changed. It’s a kind of bonus for players who have passed a level with difficulty, and also an expectation to pass next level (as the players will expect to see the next cut scene if it’s wonderful). Every time I saw the same static animation I just wanted to skip.
In the matter of sound effects, the details of audio are pretty good, as all kinds of concealed weapons and hints of danger are presented well. But the voice actors seem to be impassionate, as their voices make you sleepy. The dialogues switch between Chinese and English, which really takes away from the immersion. I think using the same language, especially Chinese, will be a better choice. The dialogues between the guards are boring because of the repetition. Actually it’s a good point to show the world view of the game through their dialogues. In my view, if guards talk more about anecdotes about the eunuchs, that will be more interesting.
Mechanics
Control System: The inconvenient keyboard control is a disaster for this action game. It made my left hand cramped, and I never got good judgments in the parkour level (I got almost all the Shadow:Gold[1] in normal level). Too many buttons are controlled by my left hand, but my right hand is free at most of the time. To a certain extent, more key controls mean more actions players can take (such as in this game players can jump, hide, slide and use gadgets, etc). Moreover, more actions mean possible to create different choices and experiences in the game. For example, in some levels of this game, I can dash between the hiding places to pass the guards, or just confuse them by gadgets. I can get the Shadow:Gold in these two different ways, and the different choices have become a kind of enjoyment in this game. These different options are built on the actions players can take. But it’s a pity that they gave us a bad default control system, and never try to optimize it or let us to rebuild it.
In my opinion, the controls can be optimized in two aspects. The first one is to simplify the key controls. For instance, now we ready gadgets by key ‘F’ and active them by ‘G’, but why not use ‘F’ only? While the ‘F’ key is down, it means ready, and up means cancel. When we want to active gadgets we can press the left mouse button, it’s a more natural and convenient way as we take aim through moving the mouse. Secondly, I suggest we can just abandon the mouse in this game, so that we are able to balance the keyboard controls by both hands, such as attacking by ‘J’ and ‘K’, crouching by ‘N’(this area is control by right hand). Further, there’s no problem to take aim by the direction keys, known as ‘WASD’.
Levels: The design of some levels is pretty clever, especially the space design. In certain houses, we can stay inside the houses, or hand on ledges, or hang on the roof. It seems that we are in 3D space but it’s a side-scroll game. But the pace of levels is too repetitive, as it’s always hiding and running. In fact the game developers had tried to explore the games storyline deeper by using collectable scrolls, however this wasn’t effective since most stories were uninteresting. Although some escape levels were added, the exciting play experience was reduced by the unreasonable key controls. What’s worse, the fighting with boss, which should be the most exciting part of a game, was designed wearily. All the players need to do is to approach the boss and kill him, without any Kung Fu fighting or animation. In conclusion, the levels are boring.
Helix: In this game we can active a special Helix state—which allows dashing between hiding places invisibly. Besides, it’s impossible to active this skill outside hiding places. This can be achieved through collecting Helix fragments to fill the Helix bar. In the difficult levels in latter part of the game, this skill offers us the opportunity to rest and change the pace, and pass a hard checkpoint smoothly. In my personal experience, it’s embarrassing to keep the bar full for a long time when there are no continuous hiding places in the level. I think it will be better if we retain the existing Helix state, but adding more features on it. For example, we can active Helix at any places, and assassinate guards won’t affect the judgment of current checkpoint [2]. That will increase the chances to use this skill and adjust the levels’ pace, which makes Helix more valuable.
To sum up, the Assassin’s Creed Chronicles China is unsatisfactory because of the impassionate voice, the bad control system, repetitive levels and imperfect special skill, etc. Personally, I hope that the legend of assassins will be staged in China again, but next time we should not only be surprised at “WOW! The leading role is a pretty girl!”

If you want more from your regular hack-n-slash RPG than just... well, hack and slash monsters and demons; that is, if you also want some good story, beautiful looking landscapes, and a dense and unique atmosphere, then this one could be for you, since it possesses all these properties. But... who knows for sure? Maybe you want even more than that these days to be convinced, something new from an old genre. Let's see...
Well...
- How about a good - and we mean GOOD - soundtrack, that perfectly - and we mean PERFECTLY - matches with that said unique atmosphere? Yes?
Check.
- How about some really nice voice acting (most of the time, at least), with European accent and all? Ok? You know van Helsing's environment is Europe, right? You remember Bram Stocker? Without google, that is. I hope so.
Ok, then, check.
- How about some little puzzles with ancient, sacred pagan objects in the middle of some frightening bog, infested with demonic beasts trying to tear your hat - and your head inside it - mercilessly apart? How about fighting some blood-thirsty, hellish fiends that jump over you out of the blue, cause you're trying to retrieve some legendary, holy, long hidden relic? How about answering some riddles - yes, we said riddles - from enigmatic NPC's, to which a wrong answer could mean a quick, but no less painful death?
Check those.
- How about some funny moments that will put a smile on your foolish face: funny references to famous games, books, movies, and characters every now and then?
Check this too.
You want all that, don't you? Man, then this game is definitely for you! Just grab it now, cause it have it all, you fool!
"Then it is perfect?" you could ask. You know, no game is perfect.
"So what's wrong with this one?" Well... hum... let's see... Ah, yes! Some skills, mainly the melee ones, aren't flashy enough. Yes. That's it. They could be more flashy. Why not? Well, they are useful, they enhance your survivability, and they are fun to use and kill stuff with, but... not enough colourful lights onto the melee skills. The ranged skills are somewhat flashy, but the melee, not so much...
Well...
If that's not enough to keep you away from the game, then...
But, to be fair, there's actually one more issue. Some people who played on easy or normal difficulty and rushed the main quest complained that the game is too short. They say 15 hours or so is too short. But... what game on easy or normal is not too short nowadays. After all, one one-shots almost anything stupid enough to cross one's way on those "difficulties". Our answer: stop playing on normal, you brainless cowards, and play games as they are supposed to be played! Your idiotic utterances do nothing but spread misinformation over the world of gaming!
Just play The Incredible Adventures of van Helsing in no other difficulty than Heroic, which is the highest one, and you're on for a fantastic and rewarding adventure that will keep you busy for a good while.
One more thing. Incredibly, this is an indie game, developed by some little known, small Hungarian group, and it's supposed to be the first part of a trilogy. So, give them your support for their making of this brilliant gem, if you like the game, and show them your interest in the subsequent ones.

Story time! I come out of a jump, right into a pirate battle as they're praying on a helpless freighter. I can attack the pirates, attack the freighter and raid for supplies while they're busy with the pirates, or just fly away. I decide to be the good guy and dog fight the pirates. When it's all over... the freighter captain offers me a reward, or to sell the freighter at a steep discount. I buy the freighter, giving me tons more inventory and I find out I can even use the basebuilding system inside.
Some time later the same thing happens again with an even bigger freighter... After so many pirates that my ship barely limped into the docking bay, the discount is so steep that, with trade in, it costs me nothing. Now I have one of these:
Ready on command to follow me anywhere I might go, bristling with turrets and with a fighter patrol to fight off any of those pesky pirates.
--
Recommended if you're experienced in the genre and have a good idea of what you're getting. It's a fun game with many neat things to find when exploring, good to play at more meditative pace. More details below, but especially if you're new to this genre, I recommend watching an LP/Streamer play it a bit so you, as said, know what you're getting.
--
The core gameplay is not too different from those like Starbound or Terraria (especially early Starbound, when you had to worry about temperature and such). Run around a planet, hit stuff with your mining laser, craft stuff, and work your way up a progression chain of what you can mine and craft. But you do have to watch environmental hazards and your life support meter. A lot of progression content is also quest gated.
If you like the survival crafting genre, overall it's a good game with a fair number of rough edges: notable number of bugs but *usually* nothing gamebreaking, and occasional crashes. It looks very nice and provides vast areas to explore, with the usual caveats of procedural generation (namely, sometimes it can feel same-ish).
The basebuilding very heavily resembles Subnautica (minus power management), and even the exocraft (land vehicles) somewhat take after the tiers of Subnautica's crafted vehicles -- so if you've played, it will feel very natural to you, but it should be intuitively simple even if you haven't. It's overall very good.

Barbarossa is the arguably the masterpiece of this series, but it was so good that I prompted me to pick up Blitzkrieg and Case blue to play the entire war.
This as the first is the most mechanically oldschool and closest to its Advanced Tactics Gold roots, which makes it also closest to a straight up 1970s style hex and counter wargame. Possibly more conservative than ATG, being more tightly bound to historical simulation, but it has been tweaked up with quite a few quality of life and AI improvements, including some ported from later games in the series. The command decision and card based RPG elements of Barbarrosa are in their earliest iteration here, so the focus of the game is still mostly about pushing chits around on hexes.
That places Blitzkrieg somewhere in complexity between the various modern Panzer General clones (Panzer Corps, Order of Battle etc) and legendary brain-meltingly complex titles with so many counters to push that most people never finish a game. In wargame terms they got the scale just right - fine grained enough to elevate it above beer and pretzels level but not so rivet countingly complex that it becomes unplayable.
It doesn't have the helpful video tutorials of later games in the series, so expect to refer to the rulebook and tinker a bit before it clicks. Speaking of clicks, it has a more clicky interface than many more streamlined wargames. As complex as it needs to be, but expect to learn a few hotkeys to make your life easier. It's a good fast-playing interface once you get used to it despite feeling initially clunky. This means you can pretty quickly play by feel once you learn the basics, and figure out more squirrely mechanics like the supply and counter stacking system at your leisure.
This makes it a great relaxed wargame to play while listening to classical radio and chilling out. You can knock out a turn or two in a single sitting without it feeling insurmountable. It hits that sweet spot between complexity and fun, each turn being a satisfying yet digestible chunk of game. I imagine this is important too in playing a sustainable play by email campaign, though I haven't tried that myself.
If you only pick up one of the Decisive Campaigns trilogy I would recommend the last - Barbarossa is a magnificent game, quite unique in the genre. But don't dismiss the first, little old Blitzkrieg, which is itself a very fine game. Vic the developer even rolled out an update today seven years after release. :)
